meta.title: NXP, Content or Cycle
meta.dek: The stock is back where it closed the night before its best day on record. What does $235 assume about how much of the recovery is content and how much is the cycle?
meta.type: Analog, microcontroller and processor semiconductors for automotive and industrial, moving to a hybrid fab model

verdict.sentence: NXP is a good franchise priced fairly for a recovery that is part content and part cycle: the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, so the answer is to wait for [[entry]] or for proof of the Bull.
verdict.breaks_if: Third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin falls below 58.5% while channel inventory climbs above 12 weeks, which would show the 2026 margin was volume and restocking rather than price and mix.

call: At [[price]] and a 20 times owner-earnings exit, NXP needs 2031 non-GAAP EPS of [[Priced-in.eps]] to earn an ordinary 10% a year. That is halfway between my Base of [[Base.eps]] and my Bull of [[Bull.eps]], and no Bear probability gets the stock to 10%. I think the market is mostly right. The business is good and the recovery is real, with a third-quarter guide that implies revenue up 18% and an operating margin near 37%. What I think it underweights is how much of 2026 is cycle. Lead times above 16 weeks, doubled customer escalations and a channel back at 11 weeks all look like an upcycle, and the $3.42 billion of the fourth quarter of 2023, at the previous peak, is only 9% below today's guide. Stock compensation and restructuring leave owner earnings at 65% of non-GAAP EPS, so the 12.8 times the Street pays on 2027 is about 20 times on owner earnings. The probability-weighted case is [[pw_ev]], or [[pw_return]] a year, below the 13% hurdle. The one number that would change the picture is third-quarter gross margin: 58.5% or better with channel inventory at 12 weeks or less says the margin is price and mix. The Bull's 22 times multiple implies perpetual growth above the Treasury yield, which I accept for the one case that is still growing 9% in year five.

tests.claim: That the 2026 recovery is content and pricing, not restocking.
tests.test: at the Q3 print (Oct 27), channel inventory ≤12 weeks, days of inventory ≤160 and a Q4 revenue guide midpoint ≥$3.75B; at the Q4 print (early February 2027), a Q1 2027 guide no more than 8% below Q4.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test1.verb]]**, entry falls to [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That the margin gain is price and mix, not only volume.
tests.test: non-GAAP gross margin ≥58.5% in Q3 (Oct 27) and in the Q4 guide, and a Q1 2027 gross-margin guide ≥58% in early February.
tests.if_fail: cut the Base to the five-year median operating margin of 34.6% (owner EPS $13.85; PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That company-specific drivers are a third of revenue and still growing 20% or more.
tests.test: on the Q3 call (Oct 27), drivers ≥ one-third of revenue growing ≥20% year on year, the physical-AI funnel above the $1.5B reported in July and data-center revenue on pace for $500M or more in 2026.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Base (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test3.verb]]**, the Bull's probability falls from 25% to 15%.

rows: Owner-earnings conversion ((CFO − maint. capex) ÷ non-GAAP NI)
five_year.note: Source: [SEC XBRL company facts](https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0001413447.json); non-GAAP operating income, EPS and free cash flow from the earnings releases (links in the guidance table). 2026E is the model's base year: H1 reported, Q3 guide midpoint, Q4 consensus. Derived rows: invested capital = equity + non-controlling interests + debt + leases − cash; NOPAT = operating income × (1 − tax), with non-GAAP NOPAT at 18% and GAAP NOPAT at the effective rate; owner earnings = operating cash flow − stock compensation − $0.58B of maintenance capex (Greenwald estimate: five-year capex less 24.5% of net PP&E to revenue times the revenue change); reinvestment = (capex − depreciation + acquisitions + change in net working capital) ÷ NOPAT; EBITDA = non-GAAP operating income + depreciation excluding intangibles. ROIIC uses year-end capital and depends on the starting point in the cycle. Net debt ÷ EBITDA for 2025 matches the company's 1.9×. NXP's own interest coverage (14.7×) uses adjusted EBITDA over net interest. n/d = not disclosed in the releases. Built with Claude.

model_build.note: Base case. Highlighted cells are inputs. NXP reports one segment and does not disclose profit by end market, so the model applies one company-wide non-GAAP operating margin to every end market; margins move linearly from the 2026 estimate (35.7%) to the 2031 input (36.5%). scenarios.note: Annual return = price change to the 2031 value plus today's [[yield]] dividend yield. Values are owner earnings per share × the exit multiple. Mobile grows 3% / 0% / −4% and Comm Infra & Other 8% / 4% / −2% in the Bull / Base / Bear; one company-wide operating margin applies to all four end markets (39.5% / 36.5% / 32%). Per-share earnings and CAGR are owner earnings per share (non-GAAP EPS is in the model-build table). The Priced-in and Hurdle rows are solved by the model along the Base→Bull path at a 20× exit. return_math.price_implied: At 10%, spot needs 2031 non-GAAP EPS of [[Priced-in.eps]] (owner earnings per share growing [[Priced-in.cagr]] a year) at a 20× owner-earnings exit, about halfway between the Base and the Bull. The perpetual form, g = r − (unlevered FCF ÷ EV), gives 10% − ($3.1B ÷ $67.0B) ≈ 5.4% [Derived], which is also above the Treasury yield.
return_math.epv: $88 per share (five-year average owner earnings of $2.2B ÷ 10% ÷ 252M shares; $98 at 9%). 63% of the price pays for growth. EPV on an enterprise basis ÷ invested capital ≈ 1.6×, so NXP is a franchise. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits above EPV because it keeps 1.7% revenue growth and a 15× multiple (implied g [[Bear.g]]); a no-growth Bear would be about $90–100.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs 9.5% nominal revenue growth for five years, about 7% real. For companies with $12–25B of sales, 36% have reached 5% real growth over five years and 15% have reached 10%, so roughly three in ten reach 7%: plausible, not probable. The Base's 6.1% (about 3.5% real) is close to the middle of the reference class (median 2.9%).
return_math.terminal_growth: Implied perpetual growth on owner earnings at 10%: Bull [[Bull.g]], Base [[Base.g]], Bear [[Bear.g]], against a 4.96% Treasury. ⚠️ The Bull is above it. It is the only case still growing near 9% in year five, and at the Base's 20× the Bull would be worth $401 and the PW EV about $282, which leaves the verb unchanged.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing in the Base: automotive content at 7% and Industrial at 8% have runway past 2031 as the S32N and S32K5 ramps run from late 2027, and a 20× owner multiple (about 13× non-GAAP EPS) does little of the work. In the Bull the growth is still near 9% in year five and the multiple is the generous part.
return_math.rr_note: Spot sits well inside the Bear–Bull range, so the ratio is not mechanically flattered; the PW case still falls short of the hurdle because the Base is only about 26% above spot.
